diagnostic_evidence.quote: $A_\omega$ is defined for any $\omega \in [0,1]$ and is continuous with respect to $\omega$ there.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the binary Fréchet mean, defined as an argmin, satisfies all requirements of Definition def:average whenever d is continuous. The paper establishes nothing of the sort: it gives no existence or uniqueness argument for the minimizer. In a general metric space the infimum need not be attained (Ω = ℝ∖{0}, x=−1, y=1, ω=1/2: the functional ((1−ω)d²(x,a)+ω d²(a,y)) has its infimum at a=0∉Ω, so A_ω is undefined) and may have several minimizers (the unit circle with the geodesic metric and antipodal x,y at ω=1/2 has two minimizers), so A_ω is not a well-defined map Ω×Ω→Ω and item 1 of Definition def:average fails. Continuity of d (automatic in any metric space) does not repair this.

failure_location.quote: It is easy to verify that if the metric $d$ is continuous as a function of its arguments, then the binary Fr\'echet mean satisfies all the requirements of Definition~\ref{def:average}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the example under hypotheses guaranteeing existence and uniqueness of the minimizer (e.g., Ω complete and the functional convex/unique geodesics), or define the average via a specified selection; nothing downstream changes.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's flagship illustrative example of its central notion (average in a CMS) is ill-defined as stated; the surrounding framework is unaffected since no labelled result relies on this example.
issues.title: Binary Fréchet-mean example is ill-defined (argmin may be empty or multivalued)
issues.why_classification: A short local addition of standard hypotheses preserves the example and every later use; no new construction or proof is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:refinement only gives R(T)_{2j},R(T)_{2j+1} ∈ [t_j,t_{j+1}); applied at j+1 it gives R(T)_{2j+2} ∈ [t_{j+1},t_{j+2}). Hence [t^{k+1}_{2j}, t^{k+1}_{2j+2}) ⊆ [t^k_j, t^k_{j+2}), not ⊆ [t^k_j, t^k_{j+1}) as claimed. For admissible rules with t^{k+1}_{2j+2} > t^k_{j+1}, the level-k interpolant at t is A_ω(p^k_{j+1},p^k_{j+2}), whose distance from p^k_j can be up to 2δ(S^k(PP)), so the third term's bound with factor 1 is unjustified (it holds only with factor 2). The same inclusion is reused in the proofs of Theorems thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType and thm:C1_m1 (the ν=0 case of the analogous display).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inclusion by [t^{k+1}_{2j},t^{k+1}_{2j+2}) ⊆ [t^k_j, t^k_{j+2}) and bound the third term by 2δ(S^k(PP)); all subsequent estimates go through with (C_S+4) in place of (C_S+3).
issues.overall_effect: The constants in the Cauchy bounds of Theorem thm:convergence and of the two proximity theorems that reuse the estimate are understated; the theorems' conclusions and rates survive once the inclusion and the constant are corrected.
issues.title: False parameter-interval inclusion makes the third-term estimate in the convergence proof unsupported
issues.why_classification: A local, routine correction of one set inclusion and one constant preserves every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee; no new argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Setting $B = C_{\PP}(S) (C_S +3) \mu^{-1}$ which is independent of $k$

issues.failure_explanation: δ(PP) is a supremum and may be ∞; for such data the contractivity inequality δ(S^L(PP)) ≤ μδ(PP) and the D-S inequality hold vacuously, so the hypotheses impose nothing on the orbit of such data, while the proof's constant C_𝒫(S)=max_ℓ δ(S^ℓ(PP)) and B are then infinite and the Cauchy argument establishes nothing. A concrete falsification: on ℝ with the primal parameterization let S(PP)_{2j}=¾p_j+¼p_{j+1}+ε·min(|p_{j+1}−p_j|,1) and S(PP)_{2j+1}=¼p_j+¾p_{j+1}+ε·min(|Δ_{j+1}|,1) with ε<¼. It is local, contractive (δ(S(PP))≤(½+2ε)δ(PP)) and D-S with C_S=¼+ε in D=Ω^ℤ (all vacuously true on data with δ=∞), yet from data with growing oscillation (e.g. p_j=(−1)^j j²) the level-k interpolants accumulate a shift of order kε, so d_∞(f^{k+1},f^k) ≥ ε and no limit curve exists. Thus the theorem as stated is false.

failure_location.quote: then it converges to a continuous limit $Q^\infty(t) \in \Omega$, $t \in \R $, from any initial data $Q^0 = (T^0,\PP^0)$ with $\PP^0 \in \D$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis δ(PP^0)<∞ (equivalently restrict D to sequences of finite displacement, which is S-invariant for these schemes); the proof's bounds are then finite and the theorem holds as intended.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's guarantee 'from any initial data with PP^0∈D' is unsupported for data with infinite δ; Proposition prop:convergence_of_intrinsic_elementary_scheme, proved by applying this theorem with D=Ω^ℤ, inherits the gap. The advertised applications (compact sets, Wasserstein) are unaffected since their natural data has finite δ.
issues.title: Convergence theorem's hypotheses are vacuous for data with δ(PP)=∞, and the conclusion fails there
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard finiteness condition on the initial data restores the proof with all conclusions, rates, and the advertised scope for the intended data; no new lemma or construction is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: d(p_{2^k j+(r-1)}^k,p_{2^k j+r}^k) \le 2^{-k} L_{\Gamma }h , \quad r \in I_k , \quad k \in \N

issues.failure_explanation: For the largest odd index r = 2^{ℓ+1}−1 (which lies in I_{ℓ+1}), the induction step needs the distance of the pair (p^ℓ_{2^ℓj+2^ℓ−1}, p^ℓ_{2^ℓ(j+1)}), i.e. the pair straddling cells j and j+1, which corresponds to r′ = 2^ℓ ∉ I_ℓ = {1,…,2^ℓ−1}. The auxiliary claim (eqn:app_induction_claim) is therefore never established at boundary indices (its base case k=1 covers only r=1, and every later top index falls outside the licensed range), so the telescoping bound d(p^0_j, p^k_{2^kj+r}) ≤ L_Γh used for the theorem is unproved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the induction to also cover the straddling pair and verify its step (the last point of cell j at level ℓ+1 is the half-average of the previous last point and the original p_{j+1}, so the straddle distance halves each level and satisfies the same 2^{−ℓ}L_Γh bound); the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:added-1 is incomplete; the statement itself survives once the missing case is supplied.
issues.title: Induction for the approximation theorem skips the boundary (straddling) pair
issues.why_classification: A single missing induction case with a routine two-line verification; all conclusions of the theorem survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, note that the power of $\eta$ scales like $\cdot/L$ with respect to the number of refinements.

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:2nd_type_prox_def bounds the difference between the L-block operators only at inputs S₁^{jL}(PP), with exponent j+1; at level ℓ the licensed exponent is ⌊(ℓ−L)/L⌋+1 = ⌊ℓ/L⌋, not ℓ−L+1. The displayed recursion in the proof of Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType (and its counterpart 2·2^ℓEη^{ℓ−L₁+1} in the proof of Theorem thm:C1_m1) uses the stronger, unlicensed rate. For Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType the final bound survives after re-indexing; for Theorem thm:C1_m1 the corrected accounting leaves a geometric rate (2^{L₁}η)^{ℓ/L₁}, which is summable only if η·2^{L₁}<1, a condition not contained in the hypotheses (η<½ only).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exponent ℓ−L+1 by ⌊(ℓ−L)/L⌋+1 (and 2η by 2·η^{1/L₁}-type block rates) and repeat the identical geometric summation; for the C¹ theorem also require η < 2^{−L₁}.
issues.overall_effect: Both proximity proofs rest on an estimate the hypotheses do not provide; Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType survives after re-indexing, while the C¹ argument additionally needs a strengthened hypothesis (tracked as a separate defect of Theorem thm:C1_m1).
issues.title: Second-type proximity decays per block, but the proofs use decay per refinement level
issues.why_classification: A local re-indexing of exponents repairs the inferences; the theorems' statements, rates, and conclusions survive with the corrected accounting.

In addition, the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} does not rely on a contractivity factor of $S_1$ and so we do not require $S_1$ to have the D-S property.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's hypotheses list only (i) common parameters, (ii) S₁(D)⊆D, (iii) order-0 second-type proximity of S₁ᴸ to S₂ᴸ, plus contractivity of S₂; displacement-safety of S₁ is assumed in the proof but never hypothesized or derived, and Remark rem:prox_2 expressly claims it is not needed. Without a bound on d(S₁^{ℓ+1}(PP)_{2j}, S₁^ℓ(PP)_j) the middle term is uncontrolled and the Cauchy argument collapses. The statement is false as stated: on ℝ with the primal parameterization, take D=Ω^ℤ and S₁=S₂ given by (S(PP))_{2j}=¾p_j+¼p_{j+1}+1, (S(PP))_{2j+1}=¼p_j+¾p_{j+1}+1. Then S₂ is contractive (δ(S(PP))=½δ(PP)), S₁(D)⊆D, and S₁ᴸ is in order-0 second-type proximity to S₂ᴸ with bound identically 0; yet from constant data the level-k interpolants equal k, so d_∞(f^{k+1},f^k)=1 and S₁ diverges.

failure_location.quote: The middle term on the RHS of~\eqref{eqn:W_proof_main} is bounded by $C_{S_1} \delta (S_1^{\ell} (\PP))$ since $S_1$ is D-S.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 'S₁ is displacement-safe in D' to Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType (and to Theorem thm:C1_m1), and remove the contrary claim in Remark rem:prox_2; the written proof then goes through verbatim, retaining the advertised strong convergence without density conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's strong-convergence guarantee for second-type proximity is unsupported and false as stated; the C¹ theorem thm:C1_m1 and hence Theorem thm:C1_manifold, whose proofs invoke it, lose their justification; Remark rem:prox_2's claim that D-S is unnecessary is wrong.
issues.title: Second-type proximity convergence theorem is false as stated: proof assumes S₁ is displacement-safe
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated, but a one-line added hypothesis (displacement-safety of S₁) makes the existing proof valid and preserves the headline guarantee (strong convergence for all of D); this is a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $S_2$ be a subdivision scheme defined on $\R^n$ that satisfies~\eqref{eqn:contractivity_diff} with a contractivity factor $\mudelta$ and a contractivity number $L_1$ in $\D \subset \big( \R^n \big)^\Z$.
Thus, the rest of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} is valid for

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The proof obtains convergence of S₁ by invoking Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType, which requires S₂ to be zero-order contractive (Definition def:contractivity); Theorem thm:C1_m1 assumes only the first-order condition (eqn:contractivity_diff), which does not imply zero-order contractivity, so the citation is outside the invoked theorem's hypotheses — and by the Chaikin-plus-offset counterexample the conclusion genuinely fails (S₁=S₂ = corner-cutting plus a constant offset satisfies (eqn:contractivity_diff) with zero proximity error, yet diverges from constant data). (ii) The divided-difference part re-runs the proof of Theorem thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType on the sequences g^ℓ = Δ(S₁^ℓPP)/2^{−ℓ}; its middle term ‖g^{ℓ+1}_{2j}−g^ℓ_j‖ requires the first-difference refinement of S₁ to be displacement-safe, which is neither hypothesized nor derivable from the point-level D-S (and deriving it needs exactly the missing first-order control). (iii) The decay accounting uses Eη^{ℓ−L₁+1} where only ≈η^{ℓ/L₁} per level is licensed, so the series converges only under η·2^{L₁}<1, not implied by η<½.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the convergence of $S_1$ is guaranteed by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence_proximity_2ndType} since $S_2$ is contractive and proximity of order $m=1$ implies proximity of order $m=0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypotheses to: S₂ zero-order contractive in D; S₁ displacement-safe in D; the first-difference refinement induced by S₁ displacement-safe in D; and the order-1 proximity with η < 2^{−L₁} (or L₁ = 1). With these, the existing proof strategy yields the C¹ conclusion, and the flagship application (Theorem thm:C1_manifold) satisfies them.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's only C¹ guarantee for second-type proximity is unsupported and false as stated; Theorem thm:C1_manifold (via Lemma lem:added-1) loses its justification.
issues.title: C¹ theorem from order-1 second-type proximity is false as stated; proof needs unstated displacement properties and a rate hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The statement is false and requires several added hypotheses plus a corrected rate; however the proof architecture (point convergence + divided-difference Cauchy argument) survives, the advertised C¹ guarantee type is retained for a standard class of schemes, and no new global proof structure is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega \subset \R^n$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and let $\D \subseteq \Omega^\Z$. Assume that for $\PP\in\D$, any pair of consecutive points has a unique geodesic curve that connects them.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts a constant C independent of the pair and of ω∈(0,1), with no hypothesis on Ω beyond completeness. This is false: on a U-shaped embedded curve (a complete Riemannian manifold), two points across the mouth at small chord distance h are joined by a geodesic that runs down the arms, and the geodesic midpoint lies at distance comparable to the arm depth from the chord midpoint, which is ≫ h²; hence no uniform quadratic bound exists. The cited Lemma 4 of wallner2005convergence is proved under proximity/curvature conditions that are not stated here, so the citation does not support the unconditional statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Lemma lemma:dist under a standard hypothesis (e.g., a uniform bound on the second fundamental form / the geodesic-chord proximity condition under which the cited lemma is proved) and carry that hypothesis through Lemma lem:added-1 and Theorem thm:C1_manifold.
issues.overall_effect: The proximity estimate on which Lemma lem:added-1 (and hence Theorem thm:C1_manifold) rests is invalid for general complete Riemannian manifolds; the C¹ claim for scheme (eqn:additional_round) is unsupported in the advertised generality.
issues.title: Lemma on geodesic vs. chord average is false without a proximity/curvature hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The fix is a contained weakening to the standard class of manifolds for which the cited estimate holds; the scheme, its convergence, and the C¹ conclusion survive there, with no new proof architecture.
